prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "planbook", with the standing line "Pours a folder of loose origin notes through one model call and casts them into the single Plan shape scaffold reads." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows An open folder spills loose pages: handwritten notes, sketches, research clippings, fragments. The pages are gathered, each with its filename tab, into one bound sheaf, the assembled prompt. From the shelf above the folder, a single genre.yaml card drops into the sheaf. So do an optional example Plan and a slip bearing the working title. The sheaf is fed into a plain press, the model. From the press emerges one ruled markdown document that flows right toward . All arrows point one way: folder to sheaf to model to Plan.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one: the genre.yaml card read for form and flavor. It flips a switch between novel and essay. circle two: the last table column, which reads Hidden Theme for essays or Subplot for novels. circle three: a ledger book where the call's cost is entered. study one: the --dry-run branch. The sheaf is shown on screen and never reaches the model. study two: config.yaml supplying the API key to the press. study three: an existing Plan laid beside the sheaf as a format reference.

Colour is used so that Warm ochre marks origin material and everything rooted in it. Slate blue marks the fixed house shape of the Plan. Brick red marks the model call, where money is spent.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 4 kinds of origin file read. 1 Plan document produced. 6 columns in the chapter table. 3 chapter types.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: Put origins on the folder, --origins on its tab, and genre.yaml on the card from the shelf above. Put --example on the reference Plan and --dry-run on the screen branch. Put config.yaml on the key card. Place Plan for Title, Thesis, Storyline in One Sentence and Summary on the document's headings. Label the table columns #, Type, Slug, Title, Hook, with Hidden Theme or Subplot on the last. Mark the Type cells chapter, introduction and epilogue. Put scaffold on the reader at the end, and cost ledger on the ledger book.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: origins folder, --origins, notes, sketches, research, fragments, genre.yaml, working title, assembled prompt, the model form and flavor, Hidden Theme, Subplot, cost ledger --dry-run, config.yaml, --example Plan for Title, Thesis, Storyline in One Sentence, Summary, scaffold Slug, Hook, chapter, introduction, epilogue

Set these short notes beside what they explain: reads the folder above for genre.yaml; every chapter rooted in origin material. novel or essay changes one column. prints the prompt without spending; example Plan matches style and structure. drops straight into design, mill runs; existing output overwritten with a warning. flat list, no Parts or Sections.
